extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for reviewers assigned to evaluate NeurIPS 2021 submissions, covering review form dimensions, conduct, conflicts, ethics flags, procedural deadlines, and evaluation scales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefly summarize the paper and its contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is not the place to critique the paper; the authors should generally agree with a well-written summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the tasks or methods new? Is the work a novel combination of well-known techniques? Is it clear how this work differs from previous contributions? Is related work adequately cited?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novel combinations of known techniques can be valuable. Reviewers should assess how the work differs from previous contributions and whether related work is cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the submission technically sound? Are claims well supported (e.g., by theoretical analysis or experimental results)? Are the methods used appropriate? Is this a complete piece of work or work in progress? Are the authors careful and honest about evaluating both strengths and weaknesses?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate technical soundness, appropriateness of methods, and adequacy of evidence supporting claims. Note whether the work is complete or exploratory, and whether authors honestly present limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the submission clearly written? Is it well organized? Does it adequately inform the reader?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not clear, make constructive suggestions for improving clarity. A superbly written paper should provide enough information for an expert reader to reproduce results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the results important? Are others likely to use the ideas or build on them? Does the submission address a difficult task better than previous work? Does it advance the state of the art in a demonstrable way?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the paper provides unique data, conclusions, or a unique theoretical/experimental approach and its likely impact on the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations and potential societal impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Have the authors adequately addressed the limitations and potential negative societal impact of their work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should generally be rewarded rather than punished for being up front about limitations and potential negative societal impact. If inadequate, include constructive suggestions for improvement. Reviewers are encouraged to think through missing critical points and provide feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical concerns (description)
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are ethical issues with this paper, describe them and the extent to which they have been acknowledged or addressed by the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should consult the NeurIPS ethics guidelines and describe ethical issues clearly for ACs and authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Needs ethics review (flag)
rubrics_metrics.description: Should this paper be sent for ethics review?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers flagged for ethics review may be assigned ethics reviewers who will effectively join the paper's assigned program committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics review area (selection)
rubrics_metrics.description: If flagged for ethics review, indicate the area(s) of expertise most useful for the ethics reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options include: Discrimination / Bias / Fairness Concerns; Inadequate Data and Algorithm Evaluation; Inappropriate Potential Applications & Impact (e.g., human rights concerns); Privacy and Security (e.g., consent); Legal Compliance (e.g., GDPR, copyright, terms of use); Research Integrity Issues (e.g., plagiarism); Responsible Research Practice (e.g., IRB, documentation, research ethics); I don't know.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall score (1–10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an overall score for the submission using the 1–10 scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score descriptors: 10 Top 5% of accepted papers, seminal paper; 9 Top 15%, strong accept; 8 Top 50% of accepted papers, clear accept; 7 Good paper, accept; 6 Marginally above acceptance threshold; 5 Marginally below acceptance threshold; 4 Ok but not good enough - rejection; 3 Clear rejection; 2 Strong rejection; 1 Trivial or wrong. Use this scale to calibrate relative standing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidence score (1–5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a confidence score for your assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 5: absolutely certain, very familiar and checked details; 4: confident but not absolute; 3: fairly confident, possible gaps; 2: willing to defend but likely gaps; 1: educated guess, not in area or difficult to understand. Use this to indicate how much weight to give your assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time spent reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: Report how much time (in hours) you spent reviewing the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is recorded on the form; being honest helps program chairs evaluate review effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of NeurIPS paper checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the included NeurIPS paper checklist as a tool when preparing your review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remember that answering “no” to some checklist questions is typically not grounds for rejection. Authors should be rewarded for being upfront about limitations or negative impact. The checklist is a diagnostic tool for reviewers to think through common issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flagging formatting and major violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not worry about minor violations of required format (e.g., exceeding page limit by a few lines), but immediately report any major violations you notice to your AC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions limited to nine content pages in NeurIPS style; additional pages for references and checklist allowed. Some extra content may be reviewed at reviewer discretion; flag violations not easily rectified without harming presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual submissions policy
rubrics_metrics.description: NeurIPS does not allow submissions identical or substantially similar to papers that are under submission to, accepted to, or published in other archival venues (including identical NeurIPS submissions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Slicing contributions too thinly is discouraged and may fall under this policy. If you suspect a dual submission, contact the corresponding AC for clarification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind reviewing policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewing process is double blind at the level of reviewers and ACs (reviewers and ACs cannot see author identities) but not at the level of SACs and program chairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are responsible for anonymizing submissions (including supplementary or linked material). If a submission is not adequately anonymized, contact the AC. Do not attempt to find author identities (e.g., by searching arXiv) — doing so would violate policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep everything relating to the review process confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use ideas, code, or results from submissions until they are public. Do not share submissions or talk about them without prior approval from program chairs. Code submitted cannot be distributed or used for other purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bidding and conflict of interest declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Read and declare conflicts of interest and bid on papers during the bidding period; bids are important for matching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check what constitutes a conflict for NeurIPS 2021 and declare it in your profile. If you don’t feel qualified to review an assigned paper, notify your AC. Deceptive bidding practices will be investigated; reviewers suspected of deceitful bidding may face ethics investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: No sub-reviewers allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Inviting a sub-reviewer to help with reviews is not allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sub-reviewers cannot be officially checked for conflicts of interest and cannot participate in discussion; reviewers must not use sub-reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer interaction with authors during discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Read author responses carefully and participate in discussion; acknowledge you have read responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors get one week to respond before discussion. Keep an open mind, even if responses don't change your opinion acknowledge consideration. Discussion period is critical for borderline papers and divergent assessments. If your evaluation changes, revise your review and explain the change. You may make comments visible to authors on the paper’s page during rolling discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to ACs and workload during AC decision period
rubrics_metrics.description: During AC initial decisions period, ACs may contact reviewers with questions; respond promptly if asked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACs make initial accept/reject recommendations; reviewer workload should be light, but promptly respond to follow-up questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting plagiarism or suspected research integrity issues
rubrics_metrics.description: If you suspect plagiarism or research integrity issues, reach out to your AC and explain the situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not handle such matters publicly; follow AC/program chair reporting channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best practices for reviewer conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: General behavioral guidance: be thoughtful, fair, useful, specific, flexible, and timely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be constructive — avoid crushing junior authors; don’t let personal feelings affect reviews; provide useful reviews to authors, other reviewers, and AC/SACs; give specific actionable feedback; be flexible to update reviews after discussion; respect deadlines. If pressured to give a particular outcome or if you notice unethical behavior, notify program chairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executing submitted code & clicking links (security)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercise caution if you plan to run submitted code or click links provided by submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run code in secure environments (Docker, VM, or isolated cloud instance). Be cautious about accessing web links, which may contain vulnerabilities or log visitor IPs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviews and meta-reviews publication policy
rubrics_metrics.description: After decisions, reviews and meta-reviews of accepted papers and opted-in rejected papers will be made public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer and SAC/AC identities will remain anonymous. Authors of rejected papers may opt in to make their reviews public; be aware that content of reviews may be visible later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contacting AC and program chairs (communication channels)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer contacting the assigned AC via OpenReview comments limited to AC visibility; contact program chairs at neurips2021pcs@gmail.com only if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments to AC are visible to SAC and PCs by default but do not trigger notifications. Refrain from writing to program chairs at their personal addresses.
